newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rice prices ease this week on low demand.
newsitem.headline: Thai rice prices ease this week on low demand.

text.p: Thai rice prices were steady to lower this week compared to the previous week on thin buying interest, trade sources said on Thursday.
The Thai benchmark 100 percent white B rice for September/October shipment was quoted at around US$338 to US$340 per tonne FOB Bangkok, compared with $340 last week.
Traders said foreign buyers were sidelined because prices of Thai rice were higher than those of of rice from Vietnam and India.
But millers disputed this, saying the foreign demand was still strong but exporters had slowed buying to pressure prices down.
"They know we have lots of rice in stock," one miller said, without elaborating. "So they try to pressure us to sell at lower prices before fresh supply enters the market in November."
According to Thai Exporters Association, Thailand exported 67,690 tonnes of rice during the week ending September 15.
